title: How to Repair a Leaky Kitchen Faucet (Ball Valve to Ceramic Cartridge) | This Old House
summary: This Old House demonstrates a kitchen faucet repair focused on a common ball-valve style faucet. The host shows how to shut off the water, access and disassemble the handle, inspect the ball and seats for wear, and replace worn seats and springs with a kit. A pencil is used to guide installation of the new seats, and a cam assembly with a gasket is installed to control travel. The top cap is reassembled and the gland nut tension adjusted to restore a tight seal. The video then contrasts the traditional ball valve with the newer ceramic-disc cartridge, explaining how ceramic discs reduce wear and can last longer, and notes that if leaks persist you can swap the entire cartridge. The takeaway is that wear parts drive leaks, and with the right parts and careful reassembly, a leaky faucet can be fixed or upgraded for improved longevity.

sections.title: Shut off water and prep for disassembly
concepts: turn off water supply to sink
remove index cap to access screw
sections.description: The repair begins with turning off the sink water, placing a rag to prevent parts from going down the drain, and removing the red/blue index cap to expose the underlying screw.

sections.title: Disassemble handle and access ball valve assembly
concepts: loosen handle screw with Allen wrench
kit tools: Allen wrench and spanner wrench
sections.description: Using the kit’s Allen wrench, the handle is removed, then the top-cap is loosened with the spanner wrench to reveal the ball valve assembly beneath.

sections.title: Observe ball seating and hot/cold orientation
sections.description: The ball sits against rubber seats; moving the handle reveals how hot and cold water mix through the two seats and how full pressure feeds through the spout.

sections.title: Remove worn valve seats and springs
sections.description: The worn seats show surface scoring (nicks) that contribute to leaks under pressure, and the springs beneath them are removed and examined.

sections.title: Install new seats, springs, and cam assembly
sections.description: New seats and springs are installed, guided by a pencil for proper seating, followed by the cam assembly and gasket, with keyways aligned to ensure correct operation range.

sections.title: Reassemble, test, and cartridge vs ball valve discussion
concepts: reassemble chrome cap and tighten gland nut
adjust gland nut tension for feel
compare ball-valve faucet to ceramic-disc cartridge
benefits of ceramic discs: fewer rubber gaskets and longevity
sections.description: The top is rebuilt, the gland nut is tensioned for a solid seal, and water is turned back on to test. The host then contrasts the classic ball-valve design with the newer ceramic-disc cartridge, noting improved longevity and the absence of rubber gaskets in the cartridge, and mentions that if leaks persist a cartridge replacement may be performed.
